\section[el ferry]{el ferry — the ferry}

\label{lesson:ES-C658-ferry}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the photocopy, then the Spanish for the consulate.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: el ferry}
\textbf{el ferry} — \textquotedblleft{}the ferry\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Tomamos el ferry a la isla.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{We took the ferry to the island.}
\end{quote}

Also \emph{el transbordador}. Plural \emph{los ferris}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{ferry} was borrowed from English \emph{ferry} (EtymDB), from Old English \emph{ferian} \textquotedblleft{}to carry, to convey\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{el ferry}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{el ferry}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{el ferry}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the photocopy, then the Spanish for the consulate, then say \emph{el ferry} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does el ferry mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The ferry\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[el crucero]{el crucero — the cruise; the cruise ship}

\label{lesson:ES-C658-crucero}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the consulate, then the Spanish for the ferry.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: el crucero}
\textbf{el crucero} — \textquotedblleft{}the cruise; the cruise ship\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Hicimos un crucero por las islas.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{We went on a cruise round the islands.}
\end{quote}

It also names the ship itself: \emph{un crucero enorme}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{crucero} is built on \emph{cruz} \textquotedblleft{}cross\textquotedblright{}, inherited from Latin \emph{crux}; a \emph{crucero} crosses the sea back and forth.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{el crucero}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{el crucero}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the consulate, then the Spanish for the ferry, then say \emph{el crucero} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does el crucero mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The cruise; the cruise ship\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[navegar]{navegar — to sail; to browse (the internet)}

\label{lesson:ES-C658-navegar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the ferry, then the Spanish for the cruise.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: navegar}
\textbf{navegar} — \textquotedblleft{}to sail; to browse (the internet)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Navegamos dos días hasta la costa.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{We sailed for two days to the coast.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Navegar por internet} — to browse the web.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{navegar} comes from Latin \emph{nāvigāre} \textquotedblleft{}to sail\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short; EtymDB), built from \emph{nāvis} \textquotedblleft{}ship\textquotedblright{} and \emph{agere} \textquotedblleft{}to drive\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the ferry, then the Spanish for the cruise, then say \emph{navegar} again

\section[el muelle]{el muelle — the quay, the dock; the spring (metal)}

\label{lesson:ES-C658-muelle}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the cruise, then the Spanish for to sail.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: el muelle}
\textbf{el muelle} — \textquotedblleft{}the quay, the dock; the spring (metal)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
El barco espera en el muelle.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The boat is waiting at the quay.}
\end{quote}

A second \emph{muelle} is a metal spring.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{muelle} for a quay comes from Catalan \emph{moll}, from Latin \emph{mōlēs} \textquotedblleft{}a mass; a dam, a pier\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short). The \emph{muelle} that means a spring is a different word, from Latin \emph{mollis} \textquotedblleft{}soft\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{el muelle}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{el muelle}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{el muelle}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the cruise, then the Spanish for to sail, then say \emph{el muelle} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[desembarcar]{desembarcar — to disembark, to go ashore; to unload}

\label{lesson:ES-C658-desembarcar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to sail, then the Spanish for the quay.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: desembarcar}
\textbf{desembarcar} — \textquotedblleft{}to disembark, to go ashore; to unload\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Desembarcamos por la tarde.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{We went ashore in the afternoon.}
\end{quote}

The opposite of \emph{embarcar}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{desembarcar} is built on \emph{embarcar} with \emph{des-} "un-"; both come from \emph{barca} \textquotedblleft{}boat\textquotedblright{}, Late Latin \emph{barca} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{desembarcar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for to sail, then the Spanish for the quay, then say \emph{desembarcar} again
\end{itemize}
